title: Clock Architecture Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: A block diagram of the five parts every clock needs (power supply, microcontroller, time source, display, and input) that relabels each block with real parts for three different clocks.

educational.topic: Clock architecture: the five blocks every clock shares
learningObjectives: Describe the job of each of the five blocks of a clock.
Compare how a 4-digit LED clock, an OLED clock with an RTC, and a smartwatch fill the same five blocks.
Explain the direction of power and data flow between the blocks.
prerequisites: Read the Clock Architecture section of Chapter 2.
Know the difference between a sensor and an actuator (Chapter 1).

accessibility.notes: Screen-reader description provided; all controls are standard HTML elements.

controls.label: Choose a clock
controls.description: Relabels every block with the part that clock uses.

controls.label: Blocks
controls.description: Shows the block job, a part note, and a link to the chapter that covers it.

controls.label: Navigation buttons
controls.description: Pan and zoom on screens 600 px or wider without capturing page scrolling.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Compare and contrast across three examples
keyQuestions: Which block is the same in all three clocks?
Why does every block need an arrow from the power supply?
What would you put in the Time Source block of a clock that must keep time when unplugged?
commonMisconceptions: Thinking the display sends data to the microcontroller. Data only flows out to the display.
Thinking the microcontroller keeps perfect time by itself. The time source block exists because it does not.
Thinking a new clock needs a new architecture. The blocks stay the same; only the parts change.
assessmentOpportunities: Students list the five blocks and the job of each.
Students explain why the Smartwatch time source can be more accurate than the 4-digit LED clock time source.
Students correctly fill all five blocks for a clock design they have not seen before.
